implementation: Expose the first rejected sequential edge, reason and admissible start-domain endpoints. Reasons distinguish run span including endpoint reach, per-member fanout domain, blocked obstacle intervals and final rounded-geometry rejection. No geometry, tolerance, search order, acceptance condition or scalar call changed.

coverage: existing edge direction/feasibility geometry and operation contracts
rounded geometry rejected on all four edges

test_correction: An initial test expected per-member fanout-domain failure for a single block with excessive endpoint reach. Inspection showed endpoint reach already participates in the earlier run-span domain; corrected that expectation without changing solver behaviour.
next_direction: Examine the south-edge run's component spans, separation requirements and eligible orientation/ordering alternatives. Interior retries cannot repair its current negative start domain. Preserve hardware access/reach constraints; do not shrink margins simply to pass.
limitations: Sequential rejection is not a global infeasibility proof.
The per-member fanout-domain branch is exposed but not separately forced by the new fixtures.
No layout, board-area or runtime improvement claimed from diagnostics alone.
Full qualification was not repeated for byte-identical output and operation receipts.
